title: Black Bean Tacos
subtitle: Spiced black beans with avocado and lime slaw
excerpt: Spiced black beans cooked down with cumin, smoked paprika and garlic, served in tacos with sliced avocado and a sharp lime and coriander slaw. The whole dish is naturally vegan and gluten-free if you use corn tortillas, which are widely available. These come together in under 30 minutes from a storecupboard base.
sourceNotes: Tacos are one of the oldest Mexican street foods, with pre-Columbian origins; black bean fillings are particularly popular in southern Mexican states such as Oaxaca and Chiapas.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The black bean filling can be made up to 2 days ahead and reheated. The slaw is best made fresh.

content.text: Serve these in corn tortillas to keep the dish fully gluten-free and vegan; flour tortillas work too but contain gluten. The slaw is simply finely shredded white cabbage dressed with lime juice, olive oil and fresh coriander. It should have a good crunch and a sharp, fresh flavour that cuts through the richness of the beans and avocado. Make the slaw at the last minute so the cabbage stays crisp.

Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Tip in the drained black beans. Add 100ml of water and stir well. Cook over a medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, mashing about a third of the beans against the side of the pan to thicken the mixture. Season and add half the lime juice.
While the beans cook, make the slaw: toss the shredded cabbage with the remaining lime juice, half the fresh coriander and a pinch of salt. It should be sharp and well-seasoned.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side. Spoon the bean mixture into each tortilla, top with sliced avocado, a pinch of the slaw and the remaining fresh coriander. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Beans were not drained thoroughly or too much water was added
items.fix: Cook uncovered on a higher heat for 2 to 3 more minutes, stirring, to let the liquid evaporate. Mash more beans to help the mixture thicken.

items.cause: The lime juice was added too far in advance, drawing water from the cabbage
items.fix: Dress the slaw just before serving. If making ahead, keep the cabbage and dressing separate and combine at the last moment.
